Finite-support graph cores are proved with the exact difference-of-output boundary formulas; the formal proof uses a different cutoff decomposition. The entropy proof specializes to explicit roots and verifies the remaining boundary factorial tail.

The integrated core energy, chain-rule failure and forward-energy distinction are separately mapped.

Full creation range, uniqueness, Poincare and compactness are proved directly from the previously established maximal coefficient graphs.

Physical tilt conjugation gives coherent-vacuum centering, shifted creation range and kernel, shifted annihilation kernel, Poincare and compactness. Gaussian one-coordinate range and kernel statements are direct unitary deductions; they do not assert injectivity of general Gaussian vector divergence.

The original divergence of the constant field is N-r and its L^(4/3)(r P_r) norm is r^(3/4). The r=n^4 ratio lies between 1/(sqrt(2)n) and 1/n. Small intensity explains the rare-count scale; only large intensity is required for the no-uniform-lower-bound result.

The count-law transfer assumes an actual count with the stated Poisson law. No stable random measure, independence of several counts, general stochastic integrand completion, new Ito isomorphism or queued research campaign is constructed or activated.

Section 10 proves the classical sharp Gaussian LSI on the entire original one-coordinate maximal weak derivative graph. This is explicitly a human extension of the named formal bounded-C1 and everywhere-differentiable results: the previously established Hermite graph core is cut off in space to form a smooth compact graph sequence, then the nonnegative K(z)=z log z-z+1 gives genuine entropy integrability and the bound by Fatou. The printed smooth-core proof uses bounded second derivatives to justify the Mehler time-generator identity and Gaussian integration by parts. The formal positive bounded-C1 proof instead uses rotated Stein interpolation, avoiding a second-derivative assumption. Both give Fisher decay at e^(-2t) and entropy constant 2 after square-root regularization.

The transported entropy is Ent_gamma((U_lambda f)^2), bounded by 2||A_lambda f||^2 for every original annihilation-domain input; coherent roots attain equality. It is not Ent_Poisson(f^2). This positive counterpart and the native Poisson obstruction use distinct nonlinear functionals.

The fixed-space recovery theorem uses an explicit positive-annulus exhaustion for the c|z|^(-5/2) mark measure and only finite-set Poisson marginal laws on one probability space. Block control mass m^4 gives input norm m^3 and terminal count L4/3 norm at most m^2. Normalized inputs have norm one while the compatible terminal classes tend to zero in both L4/3 and L4.
